judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's two headline claims are exactly right and I reproduced both: (7-3i)^2 = 49 - 42i + 9i^2 = 40 - 42i, while the conjugate product Nadia should have formed is (7-3i)(7+3i) = 49 + 9 = 58 - which is precisely the planted wrong answer; and in problem 6 the denominator (3+i)(3-i) is 10, not 8, giving 20/(3+i) = 6-2i. The rest checks too: -2-6i, 23-14i, 29, 1+2i, 3 +/- 2i, and the four zeros 2, -2, 2i, -2i. What holds me back from full agreement is an internal inconsistency the judge did not surface. The sheet's own directions say "On a 'find the mistake' problem, name the wrong move first, then redo the work correctly. Both parts are graded." Problem 4(a) is correctly given a `manual` entry for exactly that naming step - but problem 6(a) ("Explain why 8 is wrong") is structurally identical and has no manual entry, only the numeric 10. Problem 3 ("show why the result has no i in it") and problem 7 ("state how the two answers are related") are in the same position. So the sheet declares that both parts are graded and then routes only one of the two find-the-mistake explanations for review.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 4 is a genuinely elegant trap: the planted answer 58 is not a random wrong number, it is the value of the conjugate product Nadia claims to be computing, so a student who "gets 58" has performed the right rule on the wrong factor - and the declared trap says exactly that.

Problem 6's trap (denominator 8 from c^2 - d^2 instead of c^2 + d^2) isolates the single sign that makes conjugate division work, and it is declared as a machine-checked value rather than left as prose.

Problem 4(a) shows the author already knows how to write a manual entry ("Explain in words which factor Nadia should have multiplied by to get a real number") - the remedy for this case is applying that pattern consistently, not inventing it.

The progression closes the loop the misconceptions open: after two sign/conjugate traps, problems 7 and 8 make the conjugate PAIR the object of study (3 +/- 2i, then the four zeros of x^4 - 16), so the same fact is seen as an error source and as a theorem.

root_causes.description: The manual/machine split was decided per problem rather than per printed response, so one of two structurally identical find-the-mistake explanations was flagged and the other was not.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 4(a) asks "Explain what went wrong: which factor does the conjugate rule actually call for?" and verify.json id 4 does contain a `manual` entry.
worksheet.tex problem 6(a) asks "Explain why 8 is wrong, and give the correct denominator" and verify.json id 6 contains only two `eval` entries (10 and 6-2i).
Problem 3 ("show why the result has no i in it") and problem 7 ("state how the two answers are related") likewise have no manual entry.
The worksheet's own directions state that on a find-the-mistake problem "Both parts are graded".

improvements.title: Record every explanation, diagnosis and named-error item as a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat an item that asks the student to explain, justify, describe, name the wrong move, or draw/mark a representation as a MANUAL response even when a numeric part of the same problem is machine-checkable. SKILL.md and references/manual-review-aid.md should state the rule, and the response-coverage gate should scan each problem segment for imperative prose asks (Explain, Describe, Say why, Which ... did, State how, Sketch, Draw and label) and fail when the problem carries no `manual` entry. Here problem 6(a) must gain the `manual` entry problem 4(a) already has, and problems 3 and 7 need one for their "show why" and "state how they are related" asks.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem stem containing "Explain what went wrong" and a verify id holding only `eval` entries must make the gate exit non-zero; adding a `manual` entry for that problem must make it exit 0. The fixture passes every gate today, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review list delivered in final_response.md becomes true, and graders stop treating an unreviewed explanation as machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will flag scaffolding prose that is not a graded ask ("Explain to yourself why..."), so the rule needs an explicit opt-out and a short allowlist to avoid pushing authors toward manual-everything.

case_summary: Focused, correct misconception practice with two excellent planted traps - 58 as the conjugate product Nadia was not entitled to, and 8 as the difference-of-squares denominator - and a key that repairs both cleanly. All eight results recompute correctly and the study guide targets the same sign, conjugate and non-real-root confusions. The one defect is inconsistency in the verification contract: the sheet promises that the naming step of every find-the-mistake problem is graded, and only problem 4's naming step is actually routed to a human.
